plain_description.what: Applies standard multiple-testing corrections to the existing per-split chance tests, which use 300 random repeats, on four trees. The corrections are false-discovery-rate control over all splits and a nested version that only tests a split if its parent passed. The question is which splits remain certified at a stated error rate.
plain_description.why: It decides which tree splits the thesis and the talk may honestly call certified, rather than just "passed their own test".
plain_description.information: It turns a loose per-split pass/fail into a claim with a known error rate. Result: done, and the review found it valid. On the tree of record, 2 of 70 splits are certified (the splits at Chemistry and at Engineering) under the nested correction, at a per-family 5% false-discovery rate. The flat correction certifies none. The certificate does not cover the tree as a whole. 53 splits were never tested because their parent did not pass, so they are "untested", not "unreal". Only 300 repeats were used.
